behavior: One retained Rust background owner performs broker creation, stop/join and descriptor file cleanup outside GUI callbacks.
Generation/session-epoch guards reject stale completions; enabling waits for matching broker readiness and policy acknowledgement.
Disable acknowledges policy before retirement. Home Stop latches session Stop before retirement; ordinary quit waits for both terminal session and broker cleanup.

producer.checks: fmt, strict workspace all-target Clippy, workspace tests, x64 and i686 app/observer builds all passed

independent_acceptance.scope: Reviewed x64 development build: one owned GUI and EDIT target, one virtual mouse/keyboard pair, two serial connected MCP clients; Enable/connect, Disable/cleanup/EOF, re-enable/connect, Home Stop, and owned-process cleanup with later read-only absence confirmation.

accepted_core_evidence: All eleven GUI Script clicks were durably observed, including enable, disable, re-enable and Home Stop.
Both connected clients returned agent_session and routing_state under the exact sole-user/owned-PID policy with all ancillary grants false; four serial read-only calls, zero routing_input.
First client was live through disabled ACK, descriptor removal, cleanup-complete UI status and capture, then intentional EOF exited0. Re-enable created a distinct descriptor and client identity.
Home Stop reached controller_present=false, ready=false, stopping=false, successful generic stopped status, exact second descriptor absence and a fresh stopped Home capture.
Second MCP remained a live retained child until its cleanup EOF after the oracle timeout; the cleanup function only records that EOF receipt after checking it live. It exited0.

Five fresh app-owned captures matched recorded hashes; independently inspected enabled selection/grants, disabled cleanup, and stopped Home captures. 213 WM_NULL samples stayed within the approved bound, maximum203ms.

All four retained owned process handles were signaled with exit0. GUI/target cleanup path uses guarded ordinary WM_CLOSE; no ordinary_close_failures or forced cleanup was recorded. This is source-plus-receipt inference from cleanup, not a rewrite of raw ordinary_* milestone flags.

raw_results_preserved.reason: Unsupported empty ui.state Script snapshot oracle failed after Stop; the product does not emit a cleared Script state on SessionEvent::Stopped. These records are unchanged and are not relabelled.
raw_results_preserved.composed_assessment: This separate narrower assessment uses observed terminal launch/UI status, exact broker descriptor disappearance, fresh captures, read-only connected-state validation, retained process cleanup receipts and the later absence audit instead of treating the stale state file as live overlay evidence.

later_absence_confirmation.method: One separately authorized Python metadata-query subprocess; no GUI or worker launch, input, termination, deletion, or descriptor-content access.
later_absence_confirmation.timing_limit: These absence results are later observations. They do not establish their exact state at the original failure timestamp or Stop click.

limits: No claim that ui.state was cleared or that an OS-wide overlay inventory was performed. Original GUI root HWND was not persisted; later original-process absence and PID-scoped EnumWindows support its absence.
No worker-process handle proof, blocked filesystem/pipe/OS teardown tests, forced-cleanup success claim, worker-panic claim or hard cleanup-time bound.

Normal virtual-only lifecycle core only. No historical GUI-stall cause/fix, hardware/RustDesk/global-input/target-injection behavior, same-process isolation, full MouseMux Ultra parity, broad group/product completion or distribution acceptance.
No replay of the eleven-click cohort was performed to remove the unsupported oracle; native attempt001 failure and attempt002 raw failure/original NOT_ACCEPTED receipts remain preserved.
The historical intermittent GUI stall remains OPEN/P1.
Blocked startup/cleanup transitions have deterministic unit coverage; this native cohort does not exercise real blocked OS calls.
Agent connection-copy UI remains an unintegrated shadow and is not covered here.
